verdict.rationale: Codex is a coding agent documented to edit files, run commands, and run the repository's local development tools, which is the general mechanism for writing tests, fixing lint, and updating dependencies. None of the four named tasks is explicitly documented, and the dependency-configuration doc covers environment setup rather than dependency upgrades. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of test generation, lint-error fixing, merge-conflict resolution, and dependency-update workflows, plus hands-on corroboration of each.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent write tests, fix lint errors, resolve merge conflicts, and update dependencies for me

citations.quote: Start Codex in a repository to explore unfamiliar code, plan a change, edit files, and run your local development tools.
Inspect code, make changes, run commands, and automate repeatable work without leaving your terminal.
Let Codex inspect files, make edits, and run the tools already installed on your machine.
Delegate a longer task and return when it is ready.
